questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Equatorial Guinea?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Equatorial Guinea article.

questions.proof: The capital city is Ciudad de la Paz.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Equatorial Guinea?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Equatorial Guinea on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Equatorial Guinea article.

questions.proof: It borders Cameroon on the north, Gabon on the south and east, and the Gulf of Guinea on the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Equatorial Guinea?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Equatorial Guinea article.

questions.proof: Spanish is an official language because of this.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Equatorial Guinea and the peoples living there were colonized by _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “colonized”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Equatorial Guinea article.

questions.proof: Equatorial Guinea and the peoples living there were colonized by Spain.
